newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil eases, gas oil steady.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil eases, gas oil steady.

text.p: Fuel oil swaps eased as the cash market saw buyers moving to the sidelines after the recent hike in prices has dampened demand, traders said on Thursday.
March fuel oil swaps were indicated at $97.75/$99.75 per tonne, slightly lower from $99.50/$100.50 on Tuesday.
The April swap was quoted at $95.50/$96.75, also lower from $97.75/$98.50 per tonne a day ago.
"Weaker crude prices have also dampened sentiment," said one trader.
In the cash market, Chinese demand remained weak, traders said. They said traders who were pricing out their cargoes early in the week, withdrew their support since Wednesday.
Brokers said the fall in stocks have not provided the market much support. Singapore weekly residue stocks fell 1.634 million barrels in the week ending March 5 to 10.595 million barrels.
Gas oil swap quotes were largely unchanged.
"The market has also shrugged off the stock figures," said a trader.
Middle distillate stocks fell by 556,000 barrels to 6.712 million barrels.
March gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.90/$26.00 per barrel and April at $24.40/$24.60.
Meanwhile, firm jet demand has widened the March jet/gasoil spread. The March regrade was last quoted at $2.00/$2.40 per barrel, up from Wednesday's quotes at $1.90.
Singapore cash jet fuel jumped 40 cents higher on Wednesday after a trader purchased a 100,000-barrel lot from European major at $29.50 per barrel for March 20-24 lifting.
"The hike caused the regrade to widen," said a broker.
